methods: expressing area in terms of radius
statement: A closed cylindrical can of fixed volume $V$ is to be made. Show that its surface area is minimised when its height equals its diameter.
solution: Let the radius be $r$ and the height $h$. The volume condition gives $V=\\pi r^{2}h$, so $h=V/(\\pi r^{2})$. The surface area is $A=2\\pi r^{2}+2\\pi r h=2\\pi r^{2}+2V/r$. Then $\\frac{dA}{dr}=4\\pi r-2V/r^{2}$, which vanishes when $4\\pi r^{3}=2V=2\\pi r^{2}h$, i.e. $2r=h$. Since $\\frac{d^{2}A}{dr^{2}}=4\\pi+4V/r^{3}>0$, this is a minimum, so the area is least when height equals diameter.
hints: Write h in terms of r and V.
Express the total surface area as a function of r only.
